dependencies.registry: Authors' original task/language registry: exact kernel bytes, signatures, launches, reference modules, pinned operation tables, and exported proofs. Independent programs at equal shapes cannot replace these inputs.
dependencies.harness: Original proof-agent harness and prompts, segmentation/scaffolding, tool protocol, retries, stopping rules, context compaction, model settings and usage accounting.
dependencies.runs: Original request/response and checker traces, model revisions and original hosted-model outcomes. Offline/free inference does not recover historical paid or closed-model runs.
dependencies.mutants: All 42 original mutant source files, baseline bindings, rule assignments, final-run traces and rejection-channel decisions, including independent second opinions.
dependencies.production: The ten exact adapted production sources, upstream commits, ordered rewrites/departures, argument signatures and launch metadata; nine accepted full-kernel proof projects and the rejected kernel trace.
dependencies.hardware: Original optimized kernels and numerical contracts, complete fastest-vendor baselines, H100 execution for PTX/CUDA and same-device MI300X HIP measurements. MI350X measurements cannot fill H100 cells.
dependencies.semantics: Broader readers and scalable packed/tiled, arbitrary sparse-subgroup, online and combined collective proofs remain software work. Complete native multiwave activation and weighted RMSNorm profiles, aligned logical-16 cohorts inside physical wave64, single-shape MFMA and exact-real wave-sum profiles do not cover the authors' original optimized registry.
dependencies.history: Authors' source tree and development records. An independent implementation cannot recreate historical person-days, original source-line totals or original code-sharing percentages.
dependencies.gqa_export: Authors' supplementary standalone GQA proof project and its pinned toolchain/dependencies; it was not present in the inspected manuscript archive or bounded release endpoints.
dependencies.specification: Authors' elaborated Lean module formalizations, metaprogram/reference tests, accepted shape/precision contracts and associated trusted-assumption reports.

tab:instr-cats.title: Operation schemas
tab:instr-cats.available_evidence: Restricted scalar/memory/control/barrier definitions, full-wave shuffle, one native MFMA shape, and an exact-real six-stage XOR reduction with whole-launch proofs. These do not cover the full original instruction table. A complete native RMSNorm launch now composes aligned logical-16 shuffles inside physical wave64 with both block barriers; this does not cover arbitrary sparse masks or the whole original instruction table.

tab:main-results.title: Level-1 model pass rates and token means
tab:main-results.available_evidence: All twelve workload families have independent full-shape CUDA/HIP contracts; local models saw reduced HIP fixtures, not these original cells.

tab:verify-model.title: Five Level-2 PTX model results
tab:verify-model.available_evidence: Independent HIP/CUDA contracts cover the five shapes; attention is dense SDPA, not online FlashAttention, and original Level-2 PTX proofs are absent.

tab:mutation-rules.title: 42 mutants by rule and language
tab:mutation-rules.available_evidence: Several independent direct-Lean mutation studies exist; none is relabeled as the original 42 mutants or their diagnoses.

tab:lib-kernels.title: Ten production kernels: nine certificates and one race
tab:lib-kernels.available_evidence: One independent upstream-derived SiLU-and-mul family has whole native multiwave launch proofs: eight HIP/CUDA certificates/rechecks at three device shapes and two symbolic-only extremes, plus earlier small fixtures. The llm.c access-pair witness is proved. The original nine adapted certificates and rejected-kernel trace remain absent. An additional independent weighted FP16 RMSNorm adaptation has four canonical-real native certificates/rechecks and 127,008,768 earlier CPU-reference comparisons on two MI350X hosts. It is not an original production proof or the full upstream API.

tab:kernelcraft-levels.title: Task names and Level-1/Level-2 grouping
tab:kernelcraft-levels.available_evidence: The published twelve/five workload-family grouping is recorded and all seventeen shapes have independent contracts.

tab:kernelcraft-model-budgets.title: Round and spending budgets; pilot-derived setup
tab:kernelcraft-model-budgets.available_evidence: Original settings are manuscript metadata. Free local runs used explicitly different attempt/token budgets; no dollar ceiling was simulated.

tab:kernel-levels.title: Highest cut level of original kernels
tab:kernel-levels.available_evidence: Independent multiwave strided activation and a six-stage wave64 butterfly now have actual launch proofs; their shapes and phase structure do not establish the original kernels' highest-cut classification. The independent native RMSNorm proof includes the actual 1024-thread block phases and grid halt; the original kernels and their cut-level census remain missing.

tab:task-configs.title: Largest FP16 configurations for seventeen workloads
tab:task-configs.available_evidence: All seventeen published workload dimensions are exercised independently. References, precision boundaries and algorithms retain their stated differences. The separate weighted FP16 native RMSNorm profile proves width16384, block1024/wave64 and all 1<=rows<256. Its weight input and source adaptation differ from the original unweighted task.

tab:final-experiment-parameters.title: Original model/harness flags
tab:final-experiment-parameters.available_evidence: The table records the original settings, but the original harness is unavailable and local calls use a different proof-proposal protocol.

tab:eval-main-res.title: 144 Level-1 task/model/language cells
tab:eval-main-res.available_evidence: The completed local comparison has seventeen reduced HIP fixtures per open checkpoint, not the four-model, three-language original matrix.

tab:stage-cost.title: Tokens per segmentation, equivalence and diagnosis stage
tab:stage-cost.available_evidence: Local prompt/completion usage is audited; its stages and cached-dialogue accounting do not match the original stage traces.

tab:analyst-cost.title: Diagnosis calls, cost shares and second opinions
tab:analyst-cost.available_evidence: Local failed proofs and a comments-only replay are archived. They do not implement or reproduce the original analyst/probe/second-opinion census.

tab:latency.title: H100 and MI300X latency/speedup cells
tab:latency.available_evidence: Independent AMD numerical checks and timings are published, with no substitution into original hardware/kernel/vendor cells. The additional native RMSNorm study contains numerical MI350X comparisons, with signed-zero and one-half-ULP differences; these supply no H100 latency cell.

tab:mutation-channels.title: 42 mutants by final rejection channel
tab:mutation-channels.available_evidence: Independent Lean rejection is distinct from original static/race/diagnosis/premise classifications and their original counts.

tab:retarget.title: Shared and language-specific architecture
tab:retarget.available_evidence: Shared machine plus restricted CUDA/HIP/PTX readers and separate collective extensions implement an independent architectural analogue. The independent native RMSNorm profile reuses the pinned nonlinear machine and adds an aligned-partition scheduler and complete source proof; original effort and sharing measurements are not recovered.

tab:trust.title: Acceptance basis and trust boundary
tab:trust.available_evidence: Fixed source/reference statements, actual launch/RF theorems, standard-axiom audits, isolated rechecks and a pinned exact-real interpretation are implemented. Floating-point cancellation probes demonstrate the limit of interpreting real equality as IEEE equivalence. The independent native RMSNorm exports bind all 70 proof modules, closed source/reference/task statements and optional dependency pins; installed-wheel and standalone rebuild checks pass. Hardware correspondence and IEEE error bounds remain outside the proof.

fig:flowchart-compare.title: Trust comparison diagram
fig:flowchart-compare.available_evidence: An independently implemented trust boundary is documented. Re-drawing the diagram would not add empirical reproduction evidence.

fig:flowchart-detail.title: Verification workflow diagram

fig:analyst-ratios.available_evidence: Failed local attempts are retained, but original language/model/level/library analyst verdict distributions are not reproduced.

narrative.available_evidence: A comments-only replay performs no analyst intervention and is not the original diagnosis-enabled/disabled or second-opinion study.

narrative.title: Per-operation GPU semantics conformance
narrative.available_evidence: Scalar/conversion, shuffle and one MFMA shape have finite AMD evidence. Each host also matches a real-certified XOR reduction's source tree on 17,408 outputs; 128/512 cancellation outputs disagree with CPU Torch and are kept separate. Original full per-language tables/sweeps remain unavailable.

narrative.title: Historical effort, LOC and language sharing
narrative.available_evidence: Independent source counts would measure this implementation, not regenerate the authors' historical effort and original line-sharing metrics.

narrative.title: Read-back validation and formatter/reader sizes
narrative.available_evidence: Lossless source binding is implemented independently; original formatter/code-size measurements need the authors' tree. The new native RMSNorm profile regenerates its complete source/reference/task statement; tests reject refreshed-hash changes and a reference-name capture error. Original reader sizes are not reproduced.

narrative.title: Supplementary GQA standalone certificate
narrative.available_evidence: Independent GQA exports exist; the specific supplementary original project was not found in the inspected archive/endpoints.

narrative.title: Original Lean-to-Torch specification tests
narrative.available_evidence: Independent reference/AST checks include retained intermediate SiLU half rounding and a canonical-real sum. Wave-study numerical comparisons execute CPU Torch; serial FP32 reference-AST evaluation differs bitwise in 3,840 outputs. No IEEE theorem or original metaprogram-test reproduction is claimed. The new native RMSNorm profile joins actual launch correctness to a canonical-real weighted reference. This does not recover the authors' specification tests.

narrative.title: Production adaptations, departures and llm.c race/repair
narrative.available_evidence: A pinned independent scalar vLLM SiLU adaptation has source-bound native multiwave proofs and extracted-upstream comparisons. This is one family, with its source-half rounding retained. Original adapted files/revisions/departures and the full llm.c repair proof remain unavailable. The additional native weighted RMSNorm study proves the actual whole launch and canonical-real outputs, with both-host numerical validation. Its source departures are recorded independently and do not recreate the authors' rewrites.

narrative.title: Signature-derived premises, extraction and non-vacuity
narrative.available_evidence: Actual native scalar launches include partial final waves, and one full wave64 reduction has complete execution/RF proofs under its fixed disjoint-buffer interface. Original in-place, stride, packed/vector and general signature coverage is incomplete. The native RMSNorm proof quantifies over all inputs/outside memory and all 1<=rows<256 at the fixed native shape; host alignment and disjointness remain explicit assumptions.

narrative.title: Named refusal boundary and exact-operation idealizations
narrative.available_evidence: Restricted profiles refuse more forms than the paper. Real sum equality is proved for one closed program; finite cancellation disagreements explicitly prevent a floating-point-equivalence claim. Broader operations and original refusal outcomes remain unverified. Complete aligned logical-16 cohorts within physical wave64 and a complete native RMSNorm reduction are now supported. Arbitrary sparse masks, other optimized kernels and IEEE error theorems remain unsupported.

narrative.title: Race-freedom obligations and scheduling assumption
narrative.available_evidence: Per-program obligations are Lean checked; the scheduling reduction remains a declared trusted passage, not a proved hardware scheduler theorem. The complete native RMSNorm proof classifies every actual input, shared partial/scale and output access through both block epochs and derives race freedom.

narrative.title: Hints and their reported/verified status
narrative.available_evidence: Source/signature binding and trusted inputs are reported independently; the original generator/hint interface is unavailable.

scope: Every table and outer figure in the submitted preprint input graph, plus explicit non-tabulated result/method anchors. Source enumeration is mechanical; interpretation, evidence mapping and dependency assessments are authored. Rows overlap and are not a completion-percentage denominator. This audit executes no Lean, models or GPUs. It binds selected already published evidence, including the complete independent native weighted RMSNorm study at experiment-code commit 489b836. It changes no original result to reproduced and freezes its evidence for replay without a historical checkout.
